# PROCESS — what I did this iteration (explainability; REQUIRED)

**Headline: I shipped NO capability edit, and this iteration produced the one piece of evidence
the run was missing — a measured NULL CONTROL.** `cand_0003` shipped an **empty diff** (its
`prior_iterations/cand_0003/` contains a PROCESS.md and *no* `diff.patch`), i.e. a byte-identical
`prompt.md` + `task_template.md`, and the framework measured it at **val 0.975 with
`broke={50768}`**. A candidate that changed nothing lost a task. That single fact settles two
questions that three prior iterations could only argue about, and it is why there is nothing
submittable here.

## Step 0 — diagnose the MEASUREMENT before the capability (re-derived from scratch, not inherited)

My predecessor handed over "ACCEPT is arithmetically impossible". `cand_0002`'s RESULT proved that
inheriting such a claim is dangerous (`cand_0001` handed over the same claim from a *different
run's* score and was wrong). So I re-derived all of it from this iteration's own artifacts.

1. **Per-task reward table, all 40 val trajectories** (`trajectories/*.json` → `score.reward`,
   primary metric `hard_no_recalc`): **40/40 at exactly 1.0, mean 1.0000.** No partial credit
   anywhere; every `score.raw.test_case_results_no_recalc` is `[1]`. There is no failing,
   partial-credit, or communication/omission task on this split. The REAL test is unsatisfiable.
2. **The parent is stored, never re-measured.** `state.json`: `spent.metric_calls = 120` over
   `spent.iterations = 3` at `n_val = 40` ⇒ exactly 40 calls per iteration = the candidate alone.
   `spent.best_val = 1.0`, `best_id = cand_0002`.
3. **The gate rule, reconstructed and arithmetically confirmed against its own reason string.**
   `rejected.jsonl` for cand_0003: `paired Δ̄=-0.0250 <= 0.2·SE=0.0050 (SE=0.0250, n=40,
   resolvable effect size 2·SE=0.0500)`. I checked the numbers reproduce the stored parent vector:
   with 39 diffs of `0` and one of `−1`, mean `= −0.025`; sample sd `= sqrt((0.975² + 39·0.025²)/39)
   = 0.1581`; `SE = 0.1581/√40 = 0.0250`. **Exact match** — so the parent really is stored at
   per-task 1.0 on all 40, and the gate really is `ACCEPT iff Δ̄ > 0.2·SE`.
4. **Therefore:** reward is capped at 1.0, so `cand_i − parent_i ≤ 0` for every task and every
   possible candidate ⇒ `Δ̄ ≤ 0`. The best attainable outcome is a perfect 40/40 draw giving
   `Δ̄ = 0`, which the **strict** `>` rejects. **ACCEPT is impossible this iteration regardless of
   content.** This was settled in ~4 commands, before any trace was read.

## The NEW finding this iteration: the null control, and what it changes

Points 1-4 restate what `cand_0003` argued. What is new is that `cand_0003` *was* the experiment:

- **It is a true null.** No `diff.patch` was produced for it, and its own PROCESS.md records
  deliberately shipping nothing. So the artifact measured in iteration 3 is bit-identical to the
  champion's.
- **Consequence A — the impossibility is now empirical, not just arithmetic.** The identical prose
  that scored 1.000 as `cand_0002` scored 0.975 as `cand_0003`. A tie is not even the *expected*
  outcome for a perfect artifact; it is one draw among several. So a candidate that is genuinely
  *more robust* is still more likely to measure **below** the parent than to tie it. The gate
  cannot register an improvement here, and it can manufacture an apparent regression.
- **Consequence B — `LEDGER.md` row 3's `broke={50768}` is a noise artifact with a known cause,
  and the cause is not an edit.** LEDGER's own rule already says `|Δ̄| = 0.025 < 2·SE = 0.050` is
  `unresolved` and "must not be reasoned about as a regression, in either direction". The null
  control upgrades that from a statistical caution to a demonstrated fact: **zero prose change
  flipped 50768.** 50768 is also the most flake-prone task in the archive (it passed 2/5 in the
  prior run). No future iteration should attribute anything to an edit on the strength of 50768.
- **Consequence C — `rejected.jsonl` now contains an entry that refutes nothing, and future runs
  read that file as a list of refuted approaches.** Its one row (`cand_0003`) is a rejection of
  the *empty edit*. Anyone mining it for "approaches already refuted" must read the
  `diff.patch` (or its absence) first. See FRAMEWORK_IMPROVEMENTS.md.

## Why I shipped nothing — including the one edit I know is correct

**Verified-but-unshippable: the `task_template.md:97` single-cell crash.** This is a genuine defect
in the capability text I own, and it is live in **this** iteration's traces, which I confirmed
mechanically rather than by inheriting the claim:

- The snippet is still at `task_template.md:97`:
  `cells = [c.coordinate for row in graded[RNG] for c in row]`. openpyxl's
  `Worksheet.__getitem__` returns a **bare `Cell`** when the range names exactly one cell, so the
  double comprehension raises.
- Cross-tabulating "`answer_position` has a part with no `:`" against "trace contains
  `TypeError: 'Cell' object is not iterable`" over all 40 tasks: **7/7 match, 0 false positives,
  0 false negatives** — tasks `31628, 46897, 51-12, 55979, 56563, 8942, 9726`. Verbatim from
  `9726` (`answer_position = J2`), reproducing template lines 97-98 character for character:
  `---> 33 cells = [c.coordinate for row in graded[RNG] for c in row]` /
  `34 shown = cells if len(cells) <= 24 else cells[:12] + cells[-12:]` /
  `TypeError: 'Cell' object is not iterable`. **The agent copied my text; this is the
  capability's bug, not the agent's.**
- **Score recoverable on val: 0.000.** All 7 recover inside one round and score 1.0.

So the fix passes REAL-as-a-defect and SAFE and VERIFIED, but recovers nothing measurable — and
**shipping it has strictly negative expected value**, which is the part worth recording:

> The identical fix was shipped by the **prior** run's `cand_0005`, rejected at `Δ̄ = −0.025`
> (below its own `2·SE = 0.050`, and doomed anyway because its parent was at 1.000), and is now
> mis-recorded as "refuted hypothesis (a)" in two JOURNAL entries. Shipping it again here would
> guarantee a **second** rejection row in `rejected.jsonl` for the one edit in this project that
> is known-correct and known-unmeasurable — doubling a false refutation that an append-only
> handover cannot retract. Zero upside (ACCEPT impossible), real downside (permanently poisons
> this edit for every future run). **Do not ship a correct edit into a saturated gate.**

The same reasoning applies to the second latent defect (`answer_position` naming a sheet the input
workbook lacks → `wb[name]` raises `KeyError`; visible on `402-43`, which recovered). Both designs
are already written up with blast-radius analysis in `prior_iterations/cand_0003/PROCESS.md`; a
future run **with val headroom** should ship them together, first.

## Ranked cluster list

| rank | cluster | tasks | tag | leverage | action |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| — | **none** | 0 | — | **0.000** | nothing to fix: 40/40 at reward 1.0 |
| (latent) | step-3 verify snippet crashes on single-cell `answer_position` | 7 (all recover) | CONTRACT / capability-text bug | **0.000** | designed + verified, deliberately NOT shipped (see above) |
| (latent) | `wb[sheet]` KeyError when `answer_position` names an absent sheet | 1 (recovers) | KNOWLEDGE | **0.000** | designed, NOT shipped |
| (noise) | 2 unrelated one-off in-agent code errors (`7902` `KeyError: «redacted» D'`, self-authored) | 2 (both recover, reward 1.0) | not a capability defect | 0.000 | no action |

**ENVIRONMENT faults: none.** Every one of the 40 traces ran its rounds, executed its code, and
scored. The blocking fault here is not infrastructural and not prose — it is the **measurement**:
a saturated primary metric plus a never-re-measured parent plus a strict `>` gate. That is a
framework matter, filed in `FRAMEWORK_IMPROVEMENTS.md`.

## What I deliberately skipped, and why

- **Any speculative robustness/generalization edit** (the focus block invites one). It would fail
  the REAL test — no failing task on this split — and could not be ACCEPTED even if perfect. The
  prior run lost **three consecutive iterations** to exactly this reflex, each time to an edit
  that was *factually correct* (a `TypeError` guard; sheet-prefix quote-stripping). Manufacturing
  a diff because an iteration "should" produce one is the single most expensive failure mode this
  project has recorded.
- **Attacking the val→test gap** (prior run: val 1.000 vs sealed test 0.875, ≈5 of 40 held-out
  tasks). This is the only real headroom left, but it is structurally invisible from a split where
  every task passes, and the gate scores on **val** — so even a true test-split fix is rejected
  here and never reaches the champion. It needs more/harder val tasks, not a better prompt.
- **Subagents / fan-out.** The brief pushes one read-only agent per trajectory group. With zero
  failing tasks the entire signal was two cross-tabulations over all 40 traces at once plus four
  `state.json`/`rejected.jsonl` reads, and the decisive evidence was a **verbatim traceback** and
  an **absent file** — precisely what a summarising layer destroys. Fan out for breadth of audit,
  never for depth of evidence (this run's combined lesson from iterations 2 and 3).

## Files touched

- `prompt.md` — **unchanged.**
- `task_template.md` — **unchanged.** Every load-bearing placeholder is intact and untested-by-me
  because untouched.
- Handover only: this file, `JOURNAL.md`, `INSIGHTS.md`, `META_INSIGHTS.md`,
  `FRAMEWORK_IMPROVEMENTS.md`.
